clue.text: The ordinary meaning of Paine's work?

parts.note: common means ordinary, everyday
sense means meaning, as in the sense of a word

explanation.surface: A question about what Thomas Paine's writing really amounts to, in plain terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening reads like a request for a plain summary of Paine's work, but 'ordinary' and 'meaning' simply give the two words of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Paine's 1776 pamphlet urging American independence was titled Common Sense.

clue.text: Tee on high ground? (You'll never make it whole.)

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of tee on high are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A golfer's tee perched on a hill, with a warning that the hole is out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture of a tee on high ground hides the anagram: 'ground' crushes TEE ON HIGH into a fraction. 'Whole' puns on the golfer's hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction such as this is only a small part, so on its own it never adds up to a complete unit.

clue.text: The one followed wasn't necessarily the contrary type, but what did she have to eat?

definitions.text: The one followed wasn't necessarily the contrary type, but what did she have to eat?

parts.words: The one followed wasn't necessarily the contrary type, but what did she have to eat?
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme Mary whom a lamb followed to school, not Mary, Mary, quite contrary; 'had' is then read as 'ate'

explanation.walkthrough: Two nursery rhymes feature a Mary: one is 'quite contrary', the other is followed everywhere by her lamb. The joke reads the rhyme's first line with 'had' meaning 'ate'.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening line of the nursery rhyme about the girl whose pet lamb followed her to school also reads as a report of her dinner.

clue.text: Omit from 21, to form gas.

indicators.note: to form says the letters left over are rearranged to make a new word

parts.note: the answer to 21 across, a word for midday

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut something out of an earlier answer and end up with a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of OMIT out of 21 across, NOONTIME; 'to form' then rearranges the remaining NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the noble gases, the one that glows red-orange in advertising signs.

clue.text: It might make us feel a bit different, but comfortable.

indicators.note: a bit different says the letters of us feel a are rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Something might make us feel a little different yet still be comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is part of the letters to rearrange, so 'bit different' alone signals the anagram of US FEEL A.
explanation.definitionFit: Easeful is a literary adjective meaning restful, giving ease and comfort.

clue.text: Where the law was received might be in dispute.

definitions.meaning: the mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments
the ... peninsula, held by Israel and contested by Egypt when the puzzle appeared in 1975

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is biblical; the second was topical in 1975, when the Sinai peninsula was territory contested between Israel and Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is where Moses was given the commandments, and the surrounding peninsula has long been a territorial flashpoint.

clue.text: Alluded to when we tell politicians not to rock the boat?

definitions.text: Alluded to when we tell politicians not to rock the boat?

parts.words: Alluded to when we tell politicians not to rock the boat?
parts.note: the idiom 'don't rock the boat' applied to government pictures the nation as a vessel

explanation.walkthrough: Telling politicians not to rock the boat treats the country as a ship, so the boat in question is the nation itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a traditional metaphor for the nation and its government, steered like a vessel by its leaders.

clue.text: See 9 across
Hose and hoes? (They might look good to Crispin.)

definitions.text: They might look good to Crispin.

parts.note: each of these words is a rearrangement of the letters of a piece of footwear, so each one makes that word

explanation.surface: Stockings and garden tools, which apparently appeal to someone called Crispin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: things that make SHOE. Both HOSE and HOES are anagrams of SHOE. St Crispin is the patron saint of cobblers.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Crispin is the patron of cobblers, so tradesmen who craft footwear would be a welcome sight to him.

clue.text: What might be called out, with troubles on the campus.

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so one piece is set against the other

parts.note: troubles here are riots, outbreaks of disorder
a quad is the quadrangle at the heart of a college campus

explanation.surface: Police might be called out when there is trouble at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply sets the two pieces side by side. Note that the pieces do not match the answer's two words: the plural S of the troubles becomes the first letter of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A specially equipped police unit is summoned to deal with disorder, so it is literally called out.

clue.text: Evidently the girls are close, but not exactly big hits.

parts.note: near means close by
misses are girls or young women

explanation.surface: The girls are evidently close friends, though they are hardly big successes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big hits' suggests chart successes; in fact it is about shots that just fail to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot that comes close but does not strike is the opposite of a direct hit, so it is far from a big one.

clue.text: High-high, and definitely not relaxed.

parts.note: up means high, raised
tight is slang for drunk, which high can also mean

explanation.surface: Someone extremely high and anything but relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: The doubled 'High-high' asks for two different senses of high: UP, meaning raised, then TIGHT, meaning intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight is informal for tense and anxious, the opposite of being at ease.

clue.text: Certainly not a nightwatchman.

parts.note: a military post whose turn of duty is the daytime, so its holder never keeps watch at night

explanation.walkthrough: A nightwatchman guards by night; the military officer on duty for the day is his daytime opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: In the army this is the officer responsible for guard and security duties during a given day.

clue.text: Such music certainly doesn't sound like hers!

definitions.text: Such music certainly doesn't sound like hers!

parts.words: Such music certainly doesn't sound like hers!
parts.note: the religious songs named here are pronounced like 'hims', the male counterpart of hers

explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the answer is 'hims', which is plainly not 'hers'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are songs of praise sung in church services, a form of sacred music.

clue.text: See 13
Charpentier's girl, or Chevalier's.

definitions.meaning: The title heroine of Gustave Charpentier's 1900 opera
A signature song of the French singer Maurice Chevalier

explanation.walkthrough: Two Frenchmen, one opera composer and one music-hall singer, each made the same girl's name famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The same French girl's name titles both an opera and a popular song of 1929.

clue.text: It might be the last thing one offers.

definitions.text: It might be the last thing one offers.

parts.words: It might be the last thing one offers.
parts.note: a final demand with a threat attached, offered as the last term before talks break off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Last thing one offers' sounds like a parting gift, but it is the final terms in a negotiation.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a final statement of terms, whose rejection ends negotiation and may bring action.

clue.text: With Chicago thickly populated, there's still style there!

definitions.note: a clause standing for a style of architecture that survives in Chicago's buildings

indicators.note: populated says the words Chicago thickly are inhabited by the answer, which lives inside them

parts.note: the answer's letters run across the end of Chicago and the start of thickly

explanation.surface: A crowded Chicago still has plenty of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'populated' says the answer lives inside the words: chicaGO THICkly. Chicago's Tribune Tower is a famous neo-Gothic skyscraper.
explanation.definitionFit: This medieval architectural style of pointed arches was revived in American skyscrapers and campuses and is still standing there.

clue.text: What the computer might give.

parts.note: the results a machine delivers once it has processed its data

explanation.walkthrough: A plain description: what comes out of a computer after it has done its processing.
explanation.definitionFit: Output is the data or results a computer produces, as opposed to the input fed into it.

clue.text: Used to carry the torch.

parts.note: an old iron basket on a pole that held burning oil or coal for light

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry the torch' suggests unrequited love; here it is literal, a vessel that held the flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset is a metal cup or basket filled with fuel and mounted on a pole, carried or hung as a beacon.

clue.text: M. in short.

parts.note: M. is the abbreviation of the Latin meridies, midday, as in a.m. and p.m.

explanation.walkthrough: 'M.' looks like Monsieur, but it is the M of a.m. and p.m., which stands for meridiem, midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin meridies, abbreviated M., means the middle of the day, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Nothing at breakfast, for instance — except this!

definitions.text: Nothing at breakfast, for instance — except this!

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
breakfast is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: A spartan breakfast table holding just one food.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue says the only thing eaten at breakfast is porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground or rolled oats are cooked into porridge, the classic plain breakfast dish.

clue.text: See 11 across
Impressed? Beat with the feet!

definitions.meaning: struck the ground heavily with the feet

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one verb: pressing a mark onto something, and bringing the foot down hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal or die leaves an impression, and an angry child pounds the floor; both are this past tense.

clue.text: What you might deserve, in the first place.

definitions.text: What you might deserve, in the first place.

parts.words: What you might deserve, in the first place.
parts.note: finishing first earns a gold award, so 'in the first place' means for coming first

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the first place' sounds like 'originally', but it means for finishing first in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A winner is presented with a metal disc as the reward for coming first.

clue.text: It's only a theory, but I am most confused by it!

indicators.note: confused says the letters of I am most are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an idea as mere theory while admitting it baffles them.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomism is the philosophical theory that all matter is made of tiny indivisible particles.

clue.text: It might be the chain type, unless 24.

definitions.text: It might be the chain type, unless 24.

parts.words: It might be the chain type, unless 24.
parts.note: one word covers armour of linked rings and, when it carries a stamp as in 24 across, the post

explanation.walkthrough: Answer 24 across is STAMPED: the word is either chain armour or, when stamped, the post.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both armour made of interlinked metal rings and letters sent through the post.

clue.text: See 10 across
See 7 down
The 9 type might go on a pump.

definitions.text: The 9 type might go on a pump.

parts.words: The 9 type might go on a pump.
parts.note: 9 across begins with SHOE, so this is the shoe kind of a wooden thing with that name, and a pump is a light shoe

explanation.walkthrough: 9 across starts with SHOE, and a shoe tree is a form put inside a shoe to keep its shape. A pump here is a light shoe, not a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe tree is a foot-shaped block inserted into footwear, such as a pump, to hold its shape.

clue.text: See 3 down
